display.title: Episode 161: The Forbidden Road, Chapter 1
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi celebrates 160 weeks on the air and the Twelve Pesukim, and a rich man who loses his temper and fires his son's teacher walks onto a forbidden road.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi opens with a pile of listeners' letters and postcards and celebrates 160 weeks of Tzivos Hashem on the Air, inviting every child to join Tzivos Hashem and to recite the Twelve Pesukim daily. The march is set to the first of them, Torah Tziva Lanu, and is followed by the sponsor's milk commercial. A nine-year-old girl from Beis Rivka leads the Shema. Before the story Uncle Yossi teaches that what counts most is putting Torah into action, especially self-control: never lose your temper. Story time begins 'The Forbidden Road', introduced on air as 'Rabbi Beryl Learns a Lesson'. Reb Beryl is rich and learned but stingy, boastful and quick to anger. When he hears his son's melamed teach that wealth and poverty are in Hashem's hands and can change in a moment, he angrily sends the teacher away. Walking off his temper, he strays onto a street forbidden to Jews on Sundays; an officer tricks him into signing away all his property, and in one moment he is penniless. He decides to go to his Rebbe for advice, and the chapter ends there. At Mitzvah Time a caller explains that honoring parents includes grandparents.
display.lesson: Learning must lead to action: control your temper, because anger can cost you everything.
